heuristics.extrapolation: van Oorschot-Wiener 1999, the common generic-track premise, separation and priced sensitivity in proof Section 6, plus exact-program consistency checks.
heuristics.limitations: Experiments do not reach birthday scale; circuit, memory and comparator-F arithmetic do not depend on H1.
heuristics.scope: The fixed r11 chain, 93000 trails, exact DP threshold, replay cap, 256 lanes and at most 256*Tb evaluations.
heuristics.statement: H1 is one premise. Let A_g be this bounded attempt on the fixed deterministic walk g. In the real algorithm's probability space, only the fresh uniform word r is random. Let F be a uniformly random function on 256-bit values, independent of r, and let P_F = Pr_(r,F)[A_F succeeds] for the same attempt with each g evaluation replaced by lazy sampling from F. H1 asserts only the aggregate comparison Pr_r[A_g succeeds] >= P_F. Appendix A proves P_F >= 0.39. The following clauses are properties of comparator F used by that proof, not additional premises about g: outputs at distinct fresh inputs are uniform and independent; its iterates have the random-mapping first-collision law; a fresh output satisfies the exact distinguished-point predicate with its stated probability independently of prior collision bookkeeping; and after any lazy-sampling history, a fresh input maps to any fixed earlier output with probability 2^-256. H1 assigns no per-history conditional probability to deterministic g because the history determines r and hence all later g outputs. The aggregate success comparison is the only heuristic step.

heuristics.scope: The register file used by the straight-line program and the search; it affects the time and memory ledgers only, not the success bound.
heuristics.statement: Machine convention: the 256-bit word RAM of collision-frontier-v5 with a declared file of 1939 registers of 256 bits (1928 used by the straight line; the search state begins at register 1928; handler temporaries reuse dead straight-line registers above 255). An operation on register operands costs one word operation, with no load or store; every load and store of the other code is a charged word operation (proof Sections 3.6 and 4). The 62048 bytes of the file are counted as memory. The cost model fixes no register count.

heuristics.extrapolation: None statistical: a declared convention. Executed checks parse both encodings in software to validate the program and measured byte counts.
heuristics.limitations: A requirement of 32 bytes per straight-line instruction would add code memory; the success argument is unaffected.
heuristics.scope: The code rows of the memory ledger; it does not affect the success bound.
heuristics.statement: Code-memory charging convention: a declared encoding, since the cost model and the target profile fix none. The straight line and prefilter are stored in the two-address encoding of proof Section 3.6 (208906 bytes measured); the other code is stored in 994 8-byte instruction words followed by 12 literal words of 32 bytes (8336 bytes measured). The encoding determines the code bytes counted in memory.

restrictions: Two distinct 128-byte one-block messages for sha3-256-r11-prefix-v1 under the injective six-lane embedding of proof Section 2.
The bit-sliced straight line has 59372 register operations, is stored in 208857 bytes under H_code, and has SHA-256 99aca3f05459f3570803486ca941f7b2af48f1e973f31084b986780a2c1fc927.

The separate prefilter has 15 OR operations, 49 encoded bytes, destination register 1932 and SHA-256 70556574176bd68efe064c4622378fdc5bfd59aaa1cbf1618fe2451a830f5a01; the experiment executes the emitted register program.
The chained-chi table has 1,024 entries, checksum c8fa4bd9170966dc, and both shipped builders verify every selected entry against all 32 concrete row inputs before use.

The assembled other code has 994 8-byte instruction words, 12 32-byte literals, 8336 bytes and SHA-256 9aa222afa41660a79c476c811f1f4f09d7fddbcefa976a225cca9df1eb20f083; the experiment executes it and checks the all-no-DP limit halt.

Machine conventions H_reg and H_code (role supporting; the cost model and target profile fix neither; proof Section 3.6): H_reg declares 1939 registers of 256 bits, whose 62048 bytes are counted as memory; an operation on register operands costs one word operation, with no load or store, and every load and store of the other code is charged. H_code is a declared encoding: the straight line and prefilter use the measured two-address encoding (208906 bytes), while the other code uses 8-byte words plus its literal pool (8336 bytes); the encoding determines the code bytes counted in memory.
The table has 18600 words and 93000 positional 51-bit slots; every packed-field boundary is exercised.
Appendix A and the experiment certify success >= 0.39. Exact N=78992236992061376366411571340581554931467, C=2981, memory=891386 bytes, preprocessing=163967924395008 word operations.
